mainTopic: A נערה appointing a שליח for her גט, and a קטנה who accepted קידושין without her father's consent
overview: According to the רבנן, a נערה whose father is alive can receive her own גט. רבא asks רב נחמן whether she can also appoint a שליח to receive it. The גמרא shows that רבא already holds she is like her father's 'hand' and not his 'courtyard'. So the real question is whether her hand is strong enough to appoint a שליח. רב נחמן says no. A challenge from a משנה is answered by saying that the משנה speaks of a girl with no father, with words filled in. Next comes a new topic: a קטנה who accepted קידושין without her father's consent. שמואל and רב say she needs both a גט and מיאון, because we are unsure whether her father agreed. רב נחמן limits this to a case where a שידוך was arranged. עולא says she does not even need מיאון. רב כהנא challenges עולא and answers his own challenge, and רב המנונא begins another challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a young woman appoint an agent for her divorce?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a נערה can appoint a שליח to receive her גט, and frames it as hand versus courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law for a young woman: can she appoint an agent to receive her גט from her husband? Is she like her father's hand, or like her father's courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. Can a נערה send a שליח to receive her גט? It asks whether she counts as her father's 'hand' or as his 'courtyard'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a נערה can receive her own גט. The open question is how strong her role is. If she is like the father's hand, she acts like him. If she is like his courtyard, she is only a place where the גט lands.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl from age 12 until 12½, still under her father's authority
An agent who acts on someone's behalf
Her father's hand: she acts as an extension of him
Her father's courtyard: a place that acquires things for him

phrases.english: A young woman: what is the law, may she appoint an agent
to receive her bill of divorce from her husband's hand?
Is she like her father's hand,
or is she like her father's courtyard?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נערה with a living father can appoint a שליח to receive her גט, depending on whether she is like her father's hand or his courtyard.

steps.title: Spelling out the two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: If she is like the father's hand, she can appoint a שליח as he can. If she is like his courtyard, she is divorced only when the גט reaches her hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is like her father's hand, then just as her father can appoint an agent, so can she. Or maybe she is like her father's courtyard, and she is not divorced until the גט reaches her own hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each side of the question would mean in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hand is an active person, and a person can appoint a שליח. A courtyard only receives what is placed in it and cannot appoint anyone. So the 'courtyard' side means the גט must physically reach her.

phrases.english: If she is like her father's hand,
then just as her father can appoint an agent,
so too she can appoint an agent.
Or perhaps she is like her father's courtyard,
and until the bill of divorce reaches her hand
she is not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּיַד אָבִיהָ דָּמְיָא, מָה אֲבִיָּה מְשַׁוֵּי שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical meaning of the two options in the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which model applies: hand (she can appoint a שליח) or courtyard (the גט must reach her).

steps.title: רבא's own ruling about a slave holding the גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא can be unsure, since he ruled that a sleeping slave works like a guarded courtyard but an awake slave does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבא really unsure about this? But רבא said: if a husband wrote a גט and put it in the hand of his wife's slave, and the slave was asleep with her guarding him, it is a valid גט. If the slave was awake, it is not a valid גט. Why not? Because he is like a courtyard that is not guarded with her knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. It quotes another ruling of רבא that seems to settle the matter already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave acquires for his owner like a courtyard does. A courtyard works only if it is guarded for the owner. A sleeping slave she watches over is guarded by her. An awake slave moves on his own, so he is not a guarded courtyard for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard not guarded with her knowledge, which does not acquire for her

phrases.english: And is רבא really unsure about this?
But didn't רבא say:
If he wrote a bill of divorce and gave it into the hand of her slave
who is sleeping, and she is guarding him,
it is a valid bill of divorce.
If he was awake, it is not a valid bill of divorce.
If awake, why is it not a valid bill of divorce?
Because he is for her a courtyard
that is not guarded with her knowledge.
phrases.notes: An awake slave walks around on his own, so he isn't really under her watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא הָא? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא could truly be unsure about the question he just asked.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's uncertainty over whether a נערה is like her father's hand or courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's slave ruling shows that a courtyard not guarded by its owner cannot acquire. This will be applied to the נערה in the next step.

steps.title: Applying the slave ruling to the young woman
steps.stepSummary: If a נערה were like her father's courtyard, she could never receive her own גט, because she is not guarded by her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think she is like her father's courtyard, then even when the גט reaches her hand she should not be divorced. She would be a courtyard that is not guarded with her father's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It shows that the 'courtyard' side is impossible according to רבא's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An awake נערה is just like an awake slave: she moves around on her own and is not guarded by her father. If she were only his courtyard, the גט would not work even in her own hand. But we know it does work, so רבא must already hold she is like the father's hand.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with the 'courtyard' side is bigger than whether she can appoint a שליח. It would mean she could not even receive the גט herself, which contradicts the known law.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that she is like her father's courtyard,
then even when her bill of divorce reaches her hand
she should also not be divorced,
since she is a courtyard that is guarded
not with her father's knowledge!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כַּחֲצַר אָבִיהָ דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the slave ruling from step 3 to the נערה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבא's own rule, an unguarded courtyard cannot acquire, so a נערה as her father's courtyard could never receive her own גט. That contradicts the accepted law.

steps.title: The question is reframed: is her hand strong enough?
steps.stepSummary: רבא clearly holds she is like the father's hand. His real question is whether that hand is strong enough to appoint a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear to him that she is like her father's hand. This is what he was asking: is she as strong as her father's hand, so that she can appoint an agent, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by restating רבא's question. He was never unsure about hand versus courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees she acts as her father's hand to receive the גט herself. The new question is narrower: does her hand have the full power of the father, including appointing a שליח?

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he was asking

phrases.english: Rather, actually it is obvious to him
that she is like her father's hand,
and this is what he was asking:
Is she as strong as her father's hand
to appoint an agent herself, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 3-4 by reframing the original question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was unsure whether she is like her father's hand or his courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא knew she is like the father's hand. He asked only whether her hand is strong enough to appoint a שליח.

steps.title: רב נחמן: she cannot appoint an agent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that a נערה cannot appoint a שליח to receive her גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: She cannot appoint an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his answer: no, she cannot appoint a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is like her father's hand only enough to receive the גט herself. She does not have the father's full power to send someone else in her place.

keyTerms.meaning: She does not (cannot) appoint an agent

phrases.english: He said to him: She cannot appoint an agent.
phrases.notes: The one answering is רב נחמן, whom רבא asked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reframed question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נערה with a father cannot appoint a שליח to receive her גט.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about a minor girl
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: a קטנה who appoints a שליח is not divorced until the גט reaches her. This implies a נערה can appoint one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: A minor girl who said 'Receive my גט for me' is not divorced until the גט reaches her hand. That implies a young woman would be divorced through the agent!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's answer from a משנה. The משנה seems to imply that a נערה can appoint a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits only a קטנה, who is not legally competent to appoint. By implication, a נערה, who is older, can appoint a שליח. That contradicts רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Receive my bill of divorce for me
This implies that (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא challenging רב נחמן from a משנה in גיטין.

phrases.english: A minor girl who said: 'Receive my bill of divorce for me',
it is not a valid bill of divorce
until the bill of divorce reaches her hand.
This implies that for a young woman, it is a valid bill of divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a נערה cannot appoint a שליח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה restricts only a קטנה. That implies a נערה's שליח is effective.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of a girl with no father
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's implied case is a נערה who has no father, so she is in charge of herself and can appoint a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A young woman who has no father.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by limiting the משנה's implied case to a girl with no father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נערה whose father is alive is under his authority, so she cannot appoint a שליח. A נערה with no father is under her own authority, so she can. רב נחמן's ruling stands for a girl whose father is living.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

steps.whatToRemember: A נערה whose father is alive can receive her own גט, because she is like her father's hand and not his courtyard. But according to רב נחמן she cannot appoint a שליח. Only a נערה without a father can do that.

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
Where she has no father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by narrowing the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that any נערה can appoint a שליח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's implication applies only to a נערה without a father. A נערה with a living father cannot appoint a שליח.

steps.title: The end of the משנה seems to be about a girl who has a father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 8. The end of the משנה talks about a father sending a שליח, so the whole משנה seems to be about a girl who has a father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of that משנה teaches: if her father said, 'Go and receive a גט for my daughter,' and the husband wants to take it back, he cannot. This shows that the beginning of the משנה is also about a girl who has a father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8, which said the משנה is about a נערה with no father. It points to the end of the same משנה, which clearly talks about a father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the end of the משנה is about a girl who has a father, the beginning should be about the same kind of girl. Then the implied נערה in the first part has a father too. That would mean a נערה with a father can appoint her own שליח, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
To take back, to retract a decision

phrases.english: But from the fact that the end of the משנה teaches:
If her father said:
"Go and receive a גט for my daughter,"
if the husband wants to take it back,
he cannot take it back.
This shows that in the first part
we are dealing with a girl who has a father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8 using the next part of the same משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's claim that the משנה's implied נערה has no father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה speaks of a father, so the beginning must also be about a girl who has a father

steps.title: The משנה is missing words, and here is the full version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is missing words. It fills them in so that the נערה case is about a girl without a father, and the father case is added as a separate point.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: A קטנה who said 'Receive my גט for me' is not divorced until the גט reaches her hand. But a נערה is divorced as soon as her שליח gets it. When is this true? When she has no father. But if she has a father, and her father said, 'Go and receive my daughter's גט,' and the husband wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 8 by saying the משנה is missing words. It adds a line that splits the cases: no father in the first part, a father in the second part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words filled in, the first part is about a girl with no father, so she can appoint her own שליח. The father case is a new case, not the same girl. This lets רב נחמן's rule stand: a נערה who has a father cannot appoint her own שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words; the גמרא fills them in
And this is what it teaches
When is this said? (limits a rule to certain cases)
Receive my גט for me (the words used to appoint a שליח)

steps.whatToRemember: A נערה with no father can appoint a שליח to receive her גט. If she has a father, he is the one who sends the שליח. This fits רב נחמן's rule.
steps.confusionAlert: The added words do not change the משנה's law. They only make clear that the first part and the last part are about two different girls.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words
and this is what it teaches:
A minor girl who said:
"Receive my גט for me"
it is not a גט
until the גט reaches her hand.
But a young woman: it is a גט.
When is this said?
When she has no father.
But if she has a father
and her father said:
"Go and receive my daughter's גט for her,"
and the husband wants to take it back,
he cannot take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first and last parts of the משנה are about the same girl, who has a father
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is about a girl with no father; the father case is a separate added case

steps.title: שמואל: a קטנה betrothed without her father needs both a גט and מיאון
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. A קטנה became betrothed without her father's consent. שמואל rules that she needs both a גט and מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A minor girl who became betrothed without her father's consent. שמואל said: She needs a גט, and she also needs מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion with a ruling of שמואל about a קטנה who was betrothed without her father's agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a father accepts קידושין for his young daughter. Here she did it on her own, so it is unclear whether it counts. שמואל requires both ways of ending it: a גט, which ends a real marriage, and מיאון, which is a refusal that ends a marriage that is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal: a young girl declares she does not want the marriage, which ends a marriage that is only rabbinic
Without her father's knowledge or consent

phrases.english: It was stated:
A minor girl who became betrothed
without her father's consent:
שמואל said:
She needs a גט, and she needs refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: קְטַנָּה שֶׁנִּתְקַדְּשָׁה שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about a father's control over his daughter
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה betrothed without her father's consent needs both a גט and מיאון

steps.title: קרנא: needing both a גט and מיאון contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: קרנא challenges שמואל. If the קידושין were real, a גט is enough. If they were not real, מיאון is enough. Requiring both makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: קרנא said: Something here is puzzling. If she needs a גט, why does she need מיאון? If she needs מיאון, why does she need a גט?
steps.whatsHappening: קרנא attacks שמואל's ruling, saying it contradicts itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט assumes the marriage is fully real by Torah law. מיאון assumes it is only rabbinic. קרנא argues that one marriage cannot be both, so you should need only one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: There is something puzzling inside this statement
An אמורא, a judge in בבל

phrases.english: קרנא said:
There are puzzling things inside here:
If a גט, why refusal?
If refusal, why a גט?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's requirement of both a גט and מיאון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט means the marriage is real and מיאון means it is not real by Torah law, so needing both is contradictory

steps.title: The question is sent to רב with the names switched
steps.stepSummary: The scholars want an outside opinion. They switch the names of who said what and send the question to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Here, מר עוקבא and his court are in כפרי. They switched the names around and sent the question to רב.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup step. The disagreement is brought to a higher authority, רב, and his answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of settling it themselves, they send the question to רב. Because the names are switched, רב is told that שמואל was the one who asked the question.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מָר עוּקְבָא וּבֵי דִינֵיהּ בְּכַפְרִי.
phrases.english: Here, מר עוקבא and his court are in כפרי.
They switched it around,
phrases.notes: They switched the names, so רב was told that שמואל was the one asking the question.

phrases.english: and sent it before רב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הָא מָר עוּקְבָא וּבֵי דִינֵיהּ בְּכַפְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument of Steps 11 and 12 to a higher authority
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is שמואל's ruling, that she needs both a גט and מיאון, correct?

steps.title: רב swears that she needs both a גט and מיאון
steps.stepSummary: רב firmly backs the ruling that she needs both. He says it would be unthinkable for שמואל to hold otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: By God! She needs a גט and she needs מיאון. Far be it from the son of אבא בר אבא to say otherwise!
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. He swears that both a גט and מיאון are needed, supporting שמואל's real opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was told that שמואל was the one who doubted the ruling. He reacts strongly, saying שמואל, the son of אבא בר אבא, would never say such a thing. So רב supports שמואל's real view against קרנא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: And far be it from him

steps.whatToRemember: Both שמואל and רב rule that a קטנה betrothed without her father's consent needs both a גט and מיאון.

phrases.english: He said to them: By God!
She needs a גט, and she needs refusal.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַס לֵיהּ לְזַרְעֵיהּ דְּאַבָּא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: And far be it from the son of אבא בר אבא
phrases.notes: This means שמואל, whose father was אבא בר אבא.

phrases.english: that he should say such a thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב answers the question sent to him in Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She needs both a גט and מיאון, and שמואל would never say otherwise

steps.title: Why does she need both?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind needing both a גט and מיאון, which answers קרנא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא asks why both are needed, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gave the ruling but not the reason. The גמרא now wants to answer קרנא's challenge that the two contradict each other.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling confirmed in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why both a גט and מיאון are needed, given קרנא's challenge

steps.title: We are unsure whether the father agreed, so we cover both sides
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא explains that we do not know whether the father agreed. The גט covers the case where he did, and the מיאון makes clear the marriage may not have been real.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said: She needs a גט, because maybe the father agreed to the קידושין. She needs מיאון, because maybe the father did not agree. Without it, people will say that קידושין cannot take hold with her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. Both are needed because of a doubt about whether the father agreed to the קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father agreed, the קידושין are real and only a גט can end them. If he did not agree, they may not be real by Torah law. Then a גט alone would mislead people into thinking her sister is forbidden to this man. The מיאון shows that the first marriage was uncertain. This answers קרנא: there is no contradiction, only a doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: The גט and the מיאון do not contradict each other. Each one covers a different side of the doubt about whether the father agreed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common pattern: when a case is in doubt, חז"ל often require steps that cover every possibility, and also take care that people do not draw the wrong conclusion.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא son of רב איקא said:
She needs a גט
because maybe the father agreed to the betrothal.
She needs refusal
because maybe the father did not agree to the betrothal,
and people will say
that betrothal does not take hold with her sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15 and settles קרנא's challenge from Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both are needed because of a doubt about the father's agreement: the גט covers the case where he agreed, and the מיאון keeps people from wrongly thinking her sister is forbidden

steps.title: The ruling applies only when a match was arranged
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the need for both a גט and מיאון applies only when the families had already arranged a match.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: And this is only when they arranged the match.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a limit to the ruling that a girl who married herself off needs both a גט and מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said she needs a גט because her father may have agreed. רב נחמן says that worry is only realistic if a שידוך was already arranged. In that case the father probably wants this marriage. Without a שידוך, there is no reason to think he agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: they arranged the match (the families had agreed to a שידוך)
and this is only when (a phrase that adds a limit to a ruling)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
And this is only when they arranged the match.
phrases.notes: He means שמואל's ruling that she needs both a גט and מיאון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the reason given in step 16 (the father may have agreed) to a case where a שידוך was arranged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט plus מיאון is needed only when a שידוך had been arranged.

steps.title: עולא: she does not even need מיאון
steps.stepSummary: עולא says a girl who married herself off without her father does not even need מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: She does not even need מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a ruling much more lenient than שמואל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל required both a גט and מיאון. עולא says her קידושין never took effect at all. So she needs nothing to leave the marriage, not even מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: refusal: a girl married as a minor declares she does not want the marriage

phrases.english: Ulla said:
She does not even require refusal.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵיאוּן אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to שמואל's ruling as רב נחמן limited it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her קידושין are completely void, so she does not need even מיאון.

steps.title: Even if a match was arranged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether עולא's ruling applies even when a שידוך was arranged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they arranged the match?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how far עולא's leniency goes. Does it apply even in רב נחמן's case of an arranged match?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said that with a שידוך there is a real worry that the father agreed. It seems hard to say she needs nothing at all in that case. So the גמרא wants to know whether עולא is arguing even there.

phrases.english: Even though they arranged the match?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts עולא's ruling side by side with רב נחמן's limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does עולא's ruling apply even where a שידוך was arranged?

steps.title: These two statements come from different reports
steps.stepSummary: The person who reported עולא's ruling did not report רב נחמן's limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches this does not teach that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two statements do not belong together. They come from different reports.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholar who reported עולא did not hold that שמואל's ruling depends on a שידוך. In his view, שמואל required a גט and מיאון in every case. עולא disagrees with that and talks about a case with no arranged match.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying עולא is lenient even after a שידוך. It says that whoever reported עולא was not working with רב נחמן's distinction at all.

phrases.english: He who teaches this
does not teach that.
phrases.notes: "That" is רב נחמן's limit about an arranged match.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא, לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reports disagree. The one who reports עולא does not accept רב נחמן's limit, and עולא speaks of a case with no שידוך.

steps.title: Another version of עולא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: Some report that עולא said it plainly: a קטנה who married herself off without her father's knowledge does not even need מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say עולא said: A minor girl who accepted קידושין without her father's knowledge does not even need מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of עולא's words as a full, stand-alone rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, עולא is not responding to anyone. He simply states the rule in general terms, with no mention of a שידוך. That suggests it applies in every case, including when a match was arranged.

phrases.english: There are those who say that Ulla said:
A minor girl who became betrothed
without her father's knowledge –
does not even require refusal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of עולא's statement from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her קידושין are void in every case, so even מיאון is not needed.

steps.title: רב כהנא quotes a משנה about co-wives
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges עולא from a משנה in יבמות. If a forbidden relative left her husband by death, מיאון, divorce, or being an איילונית, her co-wives become permitted for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objects: And all of them, if they died, or did מיאון, or were divorced, or were found to be איילוניות, their co-wives are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא begins a challenge to עולא by quoting a משנה. Pay attention to the word "did מיאון"; the next step builds the attack on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about women who are forbidden to the יבם and whose co-wives are forbidden along with them. If the forbidden wife's marriage ended before her husband died, the co-wives are free. One way it can end is מיאון, so the משנה assumes some girls need מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: their co-wives (other wives of the same husband)
women who cannot develop or have children

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raises an objection:
And all of them, if they died, or refused,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the fifteen forbidden relatives listed at the start of יבמות.

phrases.english: or were divorced,
or were found to be ailoniot –
their rival wives are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source against עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that she does not even need מיאון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions a girl whose marriage ended through מיאון, so some girls must need מיאון. The next step argues that this girl is the kind עולא is talking about.

steps.title: The girl in the משנה must have married herself off
steps.stepSummary: If her father married her off, she would need a full גט, so the משנה must mean a girl who married herself off. And the משנה says she needs מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who married her off? If you say her father did, is מיאון enough for her? She needs a real גט! Rather, she must have married herself off, and the משנה teaches that she needs מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא finishes his challenge. He proves the girl in the משנה married herself off, which goes against עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין arranged by a father are fully valid, so מיאון cannot end them; only a גט can. Since the משנה uses מיאון, it must be a girl who married herself off. That shows such a girl needs מיאון, which contradicts עולא.
steps.whatToRemember: A father's קידושין of his minor daughter are fully valid and need a real גט. So a משנה that ends a marriage through מיאון must mean a girl who married herself off. That is the basis of רב כהנא's challenge to עולא.

phrases.english: Who betrothed her?
phrases.notes: He means the girl in the משנה who did מיאון.

phrases.english: If we say that her father betrothed her,
is refusal enough for her?!
She requires a proper bill of divorce!
Rather, is it not where she betrothed herself,
and it teaches that she requires refusal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge begun in step 22 by explaining how the משנה must be read.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that she does not even need מיאון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה cannot be about a father's קידושין, which need a full גט. So it is about a girl who married herself off, and it requires מיאון for her, which goes against עולא.

steps.title: רב כהנא answers his own challenge: she became like an orphan while her father was alive
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא resolves his own question. The משנה is talking about a girl who was already married off by her father and then widowed or divorced, so she is now treated like a יתומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same person who raised the challenge (רב כהנא) also answered it. The משנה means a case where she was treated like an orphan even though her father was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא, who just challenged עולא, now answers his own challenge. He explains that the משנה is about a special case that does not contradict עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a father marries off his daughter and she is widowed or divorced while still a קטנה, he can no longer marry her off again. She is now like a יתומה. If she then marries herself off, the marriage works only מדרבנן, so she needs מיאון. עולא was talking about a girl's first marriage, while her father still has the right to marry her off, so the משנה does not contradict him.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Like an orphan' does not mean her father died. It means her father has lost his right to marry her off, because he already did so once.

phrases.english: He raised the objection
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב כהנא, who brought the challenge from the משנה in יבמות.

phrases.english: and he resolved it:
such as where she became
like an orphan in her father's lifetime.
phrases.notes: Her father married her off once, and she was widowed or divorced while still young. Now he can't marry her off again.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge רב כהנא raised in steps 22-23 against עולא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה is read as describing a girl who is like a יתומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that any girl who married herself off needs מיאון, which would contradict עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a girl whose father already lost his right to marry her off. עולא's ruling, about a first marriage, still stands.

steps.title: רב המנונא opens a new challenge: selling a daughter to relatives
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא. The first opinion says a father may not sell his young daughter as a maidservant to relatives. רבי אלעזר says he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא raises an objection: a father may not sell his daughter to relatives. In the name of רבי אלעזר they said: he may sell her to relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא begins a new challenge against עולא by quoting a ברייתא about selling a daughter as an אמה העבריה. This step only sets up the source; the גמרא shows how it challenges עולא on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah wants the buyer of an אמה העבריה to be someone who could marry her, so the first opinion forbids selling her to a relative she may not marry. רבי אלעזר allows it. The argument against עולא will be built from this dispute next.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives (whom she is forbidden to marry)
A Jewish maidservant: a young girl sold by her father

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raises an objection:
He may not sell her to relatives.
phrases.notes: This is a ברייתא about a father selling his young daughter as a maidservant.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Elazar they said:
He may sell her to relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב כהנא's challenge was resolved, a new challenge against עולא begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that a קטנה who married herself off without her father does not even need מיאון (step 21).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At this point the ברייתא is only being quoted. How it challenges עולא is explained on the next amud.
